maria: Heads up — reworking the rollout attenuation matrix for model upgrades. the current aggressive early jump is tripping p95 on a few routes where KV cache rebuilds are heavy.
raj: Can you sketch the change you have in mind?
maria: Short version: slow the early steps, add per-route caps and a tiny burst quota so critical customers don’t see a sudden flux. also add automatic hold when p95 or error spike beyond thresholds.
olivia: +1 for hold. also propose making step duration adaptive based on latency variance so noisy endpoints get longer observation windows.
samir: For A/B tests we need sticky buckets (user_hash) — otherwise sessions get inconsistent results. also we should cap % per-customer during early steps.
maria: Draft config snippet (runtime & console should accept this shape):
```
rollout:
  steps: [0.5, 2, 10, 30, 100]            # percent of traffic at each step
  durations: ["15m", "30m", "1h", "2h", "4h"]  # observation windows
  guards:
    p95_delta: 0.15                       # hold if p95 increases >15%
    error_rate_delta: 0.005               # hold if error rate up by 0.5pp
    cpu_util_delta: 0.10                  # optional: cpu spike guard
  sticky: ["user_id", "request_id"]   # bucket stickiness order
  per_customer_max: 0.10                  # don't route >10% of a single customer during rollout
  burst_quota: 0.02                       # allow short bursts up to 2% to absorb traffic skew
  backoff_policy: "double-duration-on-variance"  # UI/runtime meaning: double duration if latency variance high
```
raj: UI/UX notes: show a compact matrix in the console that shows each step cell with: percent, duration, expected QPS delta, and a small colored health indicator (green/yellow/red) computed from evals + telemetry. clicking a cell expands the guard thresholds and links to prompt evals.
olivia: For alerts: when a hold triggers, emit a rollout.hold event with {rollout_id, step, hold_reason, metric_deltas, sample_trace_id}. SRE can wire that into incident pages.

samir: One more: private deployments should default to more conservative timings (multiply durations by 2, reduce early percents by half). ensures on-prem infra isn't overwhelmed.
maria: agree. i'll add env override and a flag in console to toggle "conservative defaults" for Private tenants. opening PRs: runtime + console + alerts. assigning: @raj console, @olivia alerts, @samir docs.
raj: will wire the matrix UI and add tooltips for per-customer caps. will also add a small "simulate" button that shows expected percent per-customer given top 10 customers.
olivia: will add rollout.hold -> alert rule and a runbook snippet.
maria: thanks all. quick followups: 1) finalize metric thresholds in the PR, 2) add unit test for stickiness hashing, 3) add telemetry tag rollout.step for traces.
raj: got it. :thumbsup:
